key_insight: Spin coating a reactive carbosilane cationic surfactant (SK) blended with an amine/alkoxyl-functional siloxane (AO) produced a stable, chemically attached hydrophobic layer on glass.
engineering_relevance: Matching reactive blend chemistry with deposition method can improve the stability and surface properties of hydrophobic glass coatings.
method: Synthesize and characterize SK, then blend with epoxide- or amine/alkoxyl-functional siloxanes.
Compare spray, spin, and dip coating while tuning composition and deposition parameters.
Assess wettability, surface energy, morphology, and chemistry using contact angles, AFM, XPS, Raman microscopy, and solubility-parameter calculations.
evidence_signal: The abstract identifies spin-coated SK/AO as optimal, while spray coating yielded extreme roughness and dip coating showed limited stability associated with separated SK deposits.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative contact angles or long-term durability results, limiting assessment of application readiness.
paper_title: Custom-Designed Carbosilane-Based Reactive Surfactants for Surface Hydrophobization─AFM, Raman Microscopy, and XPS Investigations
